questionText: What is the worst case time complexity of inserting $n^2$ elements into an AVL-tree with $n$ elements initially?
explanation:
Step 1: Time complexity of single insertion in an AVL tree
An AVL tree with $k$ nodes has a height of $O(\log k)$. Therefore, inserting a single element into an AVL tree containing $k$ nodes takes $O(\log k)$ time in the worst case.

Step 2: Calculate overall insertion time for $n^2$ elements
Initially, the AVL tree contains $n$ elements. As $n^2$ elements are inserted, the tree size increases from $n$ to $n + n^2$.

For the $i$-th insertion (where $1 \le i \le n^2$), the number of nodes in the tree is $n + i - 1$. The time taken for this insertion is $\Theta(\log(n + i))$.

Since $\log n \le \log(n + i) \le \log(n + n^2) = \Theta(\log n)$, each of the $n^2$ insertions takes $\Theta(\log n)$ time.

Step 3: Total worst-case time complexity
Total Time = $\sum_{i=1}^{n^2} \Theta(\log(n + i)) = n^2 \times \Theta(\log n) = \Theta(n^2 \log n)$.

Hence, the correct option is C.
